stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Sweep each of the three sliders and watch how the hovering puck moves. Advance once every slider has covered at least half its range.
stages.concept: A permanent-magnet puck hovers over a coil. Two forces act on it: its weight $P = m\,g$ pointing down, and a repulsive magnetic force $F_{rep}(h) = F_0/h^2$ pointing up, where $F_0 = C \cdot N \cdot I$ collects the coil geometry, its number of turns $N$, and its current $I$. Equilibrium sits at the height where $F_{rep}(h) = P$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: A target hover height is drawn as a dashed line. Tune $I$, $N$ and $m$ until the puck sits on the line.
stages.concept: The equilibrium height is $h^{*} = \sqrt{F_0/(m\,g)} = \sqrt{C\,N\,I/(m\,g)}$. Many parameter triples give the same $h^{*}$ — you can trade current against turns or against mass.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The puck and its force arrows are hidden. Only the target height remains. Compute a valid current $I$ on paper for a mass and turn count of your choice, then set the sliders and finish.
stages.concept: Inverse: from $h^{*2} = C\,N\,I/(m\,g)$ you get $I = m\,g\,h^{*2}/(C\,N)$. Pick $m$ and $N$ first, then compute $I$. Values are in SI: $m$ in kg (convert from grams), $h^{*}$ in metres.

labels.tip1: sweep each slider — cover at least half of its range
labels.tip2: raise F_rep or lower m·g until the puck reaches the dashed line
labels.tip3: compute I on paper, then set the sliders and finish
labels.peek_tip_formula: Rearrange F_0/h*^2 = m g  ->  I = m g h*^2 / (C N).  Pick m and N first, then compute I.
labels.peek_tip_anchor: At h* = 10 cm with m = 20 g you need C N I ~ 2e-3 N m^2.  With C = 5e-6, that means N I ~ 400.

1.1: Which slider changes the hover height the fastest? Try one at a time.
1.2: Increasing I or N raises F_0, which lifts the puck. Increasing m adds weight and lowers it.
1.3: Halving m at fixed I and N multiplies the hover height by sqrt(2). Halving I divides it by sqrt(2).

2.1: Read the target height off the dashed line before touching the sliders.
2.2: Fix m and N at round values, then move I to bring the puck to the line.
2.3: You can freeze N and m at their defaults and adjust I only — that leaves one unknown.

3.1: Write down the equilibrium condition F_0/h*^2 = m g on paper before touching sliders.
3.2: Substitute h* (metres!) into I = m g h*^2 / (C N). Try m = 20 g, N = 300 first.
3.3: Peek gives you the rearranged formula. Plug in your chosen m and N, get I, then read the sliders.
